audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart and the prose disagree on five of seven stages. The chart reads Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Zaahen / Skill / Zaahen, while the whys say level 2 is Zaahen's spike, 'Level 3 is his', 'Levels 4-5 stay Zaahen's', 'At 6 it's even', and 'First item is his'. Only level 1 and 2+ items agree.
audit.why: This is not a single stray string — the chart says even where the prose says Zaahen owns the stage, and says Zaahen where the prose says even. I could not tell which side was generated correctly, and 1079 games is by far the largest sample in this slice, so guessing a side would put an invented power shift in front of a lot of readers. Flagged for the user instead; I corrected only the mechanics.
audit.corrected: NOT APPLIED — raised as a question.

audit.why: Zaahen's level 2 gap-close, Akshan's level 6, Zaahen's first-item duel spike, and his 2+ item sidelane control. Four spikes, correctly owned; only the mechanics inside them were wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two problems. (1) The entry says twice that 'his Q out-ranges your poke'. The Darkin Glaive is an attack modifier — it makes his NEXT ATTACK slash twice and heal him, with a recast that turns the following attack into a knockup. It has no independent range; the kit file's 25000 figure is a self-cast artifact, not a threat range, and it cannot out-range an 850 Avengerang. (2) Dreaded Return does not appear anywhere in the entry, and it is the ability that actually catches Akshan: an 850-range stab that PULLS the target to him.
audit.why: Riot's text for The Darkin Glaive: 'Zaahen slashes twice on his next attack, dealing bonus damage and healing himself. Zaahen can recast this ability to have his next attack deal bonus damage and knock up his target.' Riot's text for Dreaded Return: 'stabs in a direction, damaging enemies hit, then pulls them toward him', range 850, 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s. An Akshan told the danger is a long-range Q will stand at his own maximum poke range and be pulled out of it — the correct read is that 850 IS his engage range, so max-range poke is not automatically safe.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive is an empowered double-hit auto that heals, recastable into a knockup, on 10s. Dreaded Return (W) is the real catch: 850 range, 14s, and it pulls you to him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aureate Rush is referenced four times with no cooldown, in an entry whose entire instruction is 'commit when his gap-close is down'.
audit.why: Aureate Rush is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s and Dreaded Return 14s at rank 1. Without those numbers 'when his gap-close is down' is unactionable — the reader has no idea whether that is a two-second or a twenty-second window.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds call despite 'his sustain beats your lethality poke flat' being the stated reason Akshan loses the duel, and no mention of his revive.
audit.why: The Darkin Glaive heals on use and Grim Deliverance heals for a portion of damage dealt, so anti-heal is the direct answer to the sentence the entry already writes. Cultivation of War also lets him REVIVE at full Determination, which means securing a kill is not necessarily securing the fight — relevant to a champion whose own identity is built on revives.
audit.corrected: Stated in mid, late and whys[5].

edits.before: His spike — his E reaches you before Heroic Swing is charged and there's no escape once he's on you. Respect the wave state.
edits.after: His spike — Aureate Rush (E) lands on a 10s cooldown before Heroic Swing is charged, and there is no escape after. Respect the wave.

edits.before: Open even — poke from max range while he farms outside grapple reach. The lane turns at level 2: his E reaches you before Heroic Swing is charged and you cannot escape the all-in, so respect the wave state and hug turret through 2-5. His Q outranges your poke and he punishes every cooldown; just survive.
edits.after: Open even — poke from max range while he farms outside grapple reach. The lane turns at level 2: Aureate Rush (E) is a 10s dash that arrives before Heroic Swing is charged. Worse is Dreaded Return (W), an 850-range stab that PULLS you in, so your own Q range is not safe ground. Hug turret and survive 2-5.

edits.before: Level 6 finally gives you a fair fight — Comeuppance adds real burst — but the channel is interruptible, so open it only when his gap-close is down or from behind cover. Do not straight-duel him at first item; his sustain and tankiness beat your lethality poke flat. Chip, kite, and call your jungler.
edits.after: Level 6 finally gives you a fair fight — Comeuppance adds real burst — but the channel is interruptible, and The Darkin Glaive (Q) recasts into a knockup that cuts it, so open only once his 10s gap-close is spent. Do not straight-duel at first item; Q and R both heal him through your poke. Chip, kite, buy anti-heal.

edits.before: He wins the sidelane and he knows it: two-plus items he out-pressures you and takes towers whenever you roam off to revive someone. Pick revives that trade up, shove the wave before you leave, and use your range in teamfights — poke him down before he ever reaches your line.
edits.after: He wins the sidelane: two-plus items he out-pressures you and takes towers whenever you roam to revive. His own passive revives him at full Determination, so one kill may not settle it. Bring Grievous Wounds for the Q and R heals, shove before you leave, and poke him down before he reaches your line.

edits.before: Zaahen spikes at 2: his E reaches you before Heroic Swing is even charged, and once he's on you there is no escape. Give ground.
edits.after: Zaahen spikes at 2: Aureate Rush (E) is a 10s dash that lands before Heroic Swing is charged, and once he is on you there is no escape.

edits.before: Level 3 is his — his Q out-ranges your poke and you have no answer to the walk-up once your cooldowns are shown.
edits.after: Level 3 is his — Dreaded Return (W) pulls you from 850, so your own Q range sits inside his engage, not outside it.

edits.before: First item is his: sustain and tankiness beat your lethality poke in any straight duel. Refuse the 1v1 and chip from range.
edits.after: First item is his: The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance both heal him through your poke. Refuse the 1v1, chip, buy anti-heal.

notes: Dreaded Return is absent from this entry entirely, and it is the ability that decides the matchup: an 850-range stab that pulls Akshan to him. The page instead told the reader to 'poke from max range' and blamed a long-range Q — but The Darkin Glaive is an attack modifier with no independent range (the kit file's 25000 is a self-cast artifact), so the reader was being warned about the wrong ability and reassured about a distance that is exactly Zaahen's engage range. Added Aureate Rush at 10s and Dreaded Return at 14s so 'when his gap-close is down' means something, plus the anti-heal buy and his Determination revive. This entry's strings are noticeably shorter than the rest of the Akshan file (wants lists are three or four words each), which limits how much can be added within the length band.
unverified: The claim that Comeuppance's channel is interruptible is pre-existing text I left in place. Akshan's kit file lists needsResearch.animationCancels as null, so I could not confirm it locally and did not extend or strengthen the claim — I only noted that Zaahen's Q recast knockup is the tool that would do it.
